newsitem.title: USA: AIG's Greenberg seen as heir apparent.
newsitem.headline: AIG's Greenberg seen as heir apparent.

text.p: The promotion of Evan Greenberg to president of American International Group Inc on Wednesday confirms him as the leading candidate to succeed his father Maurice as the head of the company, analysts said.
"Evan's the guy who's obviously being set up to run the thing and it's just a question of exactly when," Dillon Read analyst Michael Lewis said.
And that may still be awhile, analysts said, noting that the AIG chief executive is in good health and apparently still enjoying the job.
"He's a young 71, as they say," Lewis said.
Indeed, Greenberg made clear at the company's annual meeting on Wednesday that he will continue to run the company as usual.
"This does not mean I'm changing my role in any way in the company," Greenberg told the annual meeting.
And analysts said they believed Greenberg would continue as the chief executive of the big New York-based insurer for at least three or four more years, possibly more.
But the announcement appears to lay the groundwork for a succession when Greenberg does decide to retire, they said.

"That's one of the few areas of uncertainty and I think that this move sounds like it goes a long way towards at least showing a succession game plan when and if Mr. Greenberg retires," one industry source said.
However, analysts said they were not surprised by Evan Greenberg's promotion.
"I think it's just formalizing what everybody knew," Nutmeg Securities analyst Ira Zuckerman said."
However, Evan Greenberg's promotion appears to diminish the chances of Thomas Tizzio, 59, taking the helm of the company, analysts said.
Tizzio, who had been president of AIG, was named to the new position of senior vice chairman, focusing on the company's worldwide general insurance business.
Although Tizzio will still play an important role in AIG, Zuckerman said, he considers Evan Greenberg, 42, the heir apparent.
That became clear, he said, after Evan's older brother Jeffrey, who had been viewed as likely to succeed his father, resigned from the company two years ago.
A number of other top lieutenants have also moved on to other important posts outside the company in the last few years as the succession issue remained unresolved.

Others who have left include William Smith, who replaced Jeffrey Greenberg after his resignation, and is now president and chief operating officer Kemper Insurance Cos and Brian Duperreault, now chief executive of ACE Ltd.
With this promotion, Evan, who has been with AIG since 1975, becomes chief operating officer as well as president.
